Subject: Trail tips for your next trip out
Preview: A few things worth knowing before you head out this season.
Body: Hey,

This season marks a real shift for us at Northbay Supply — more on that soon — but right now we want to focus on what matters most: helping you have a good trip.

A few trail tips we keep coming back to:

**Pace your water, not just your miles.**
Most people underestimate water needs on exposed ridgelines. A general field rule: 500 ml per hour in moderate temps, more above 80°F or on sustained climbs. Carry more than you think you need on out-and-back routes where there's no bailout to a water source.

**Layer for the descent, not the ascent.**
You'll be warm moving uphill. Pack your insulation where you can reach it without dropping your pack — you'll want it the moment you stop at the summit or hit the shaded north-facing trail on the way down.

**Check your footwear grip before the trailhead, not on the trail.**
Worn lug depth on trail shoes affects traction on wet root and rock more than most people expect. Run your thumb across the lugs. If they feel rounded rather than edged, plan around that.

**Know your bailout before you need it.**
Before any trip, identify the closest exit point at the halfway mark. Weather moves faster than forecasts at elevation. Having that decision made in advance means you make it with a clear head.

We're glad you've been spending time with us this season. More to come from Northbay — for now, go check what your local forecast looks like for the weekend.
